title: Zero Conditional: Cause and Effect — Quiz 83
content:
## Zero Conditional: Cause and Effect

Choose verb forms for facts and general truths.

### Lesson focus

1. If you ___ butter, it melts. (heat / will heat)
2. Students ___ fast if the teacher is competent. (learn / will learn)
3. If a young plant doesn't get water, it ___ . (dies / will die)
4. If you ___ harder, you feel happier. (will work / work)

### Understand the pattern

The zero conditional describes a general relationship or a repeated consequence. It commonly uses present simple in both clauses. Unlike a first conditional, it does not focus on one particular possible future occasion.

### Worked answers and explanation

1. heat
2. learn
3. dies
4. work

The choices fit the general meanings of these practice sentences. Context still matters: 'If the plant doesn't get water tonight, it will die' would be a natural first conditional about a specific future risk.

### Try another

Complete for a general routine: If the alarm ___, the staff check the door. (ring)

### Suggested answer

Rings. Present simple in both clauses describes the usual response. The singular subject the alarm requires rings.
